title: SSH / Remote Execution Surface Audit v1

current_state.summary: SSH does not exist in Rig Relay. No remote execution model. No SSH key management. No command allowlisting. No session recording. No remote evidence collection. RuntimeSupervisor is local-only and uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with NO shell. There is no remote variant. Subprocess supervision works only for local commands.

ssh_doctrine: SSH must never become an ungoverned remote shell for agents. No 'open an SSH session and do whatever'.
SSH commands must be wrapped in receipt-producing, policy-gated invocations — same as local subprocess supervision.
Remote state must be reflected into canonical evidence artifacts — remote mutations produce the same receipts as local mutations.
Credentials and keys must never enter telemetry, debug bundles, or evidence artifacts — content-light always.
Remote mutation must require explicit scope and approval — same approval gates as any governed mutation.
SSH should support read-only diagnostics before any mutation — run checks, audit state, verify connectivity before allowing writes.
SSH is a transport, not a trust boundary bypass — all Rig Relay governance gates apply regardless of transport.

ssh_use_cases.description: Developer connects to remote dev box. Rig Relay on local machine drives agent operations on remote box via SSH-wrapped subprocess supervision. Agent tools (read, write, bash) execute on remote but are governed locally. Evidence artifacts stored locally.

Hosted Rig Relay instance manages a fleet of worker machines via SSH. Workers execute governed subagent tasks. Each worker has its own evidence artifacts reported back to hosted instance. Workers never have direct GitHub access — only through hosted instance governance.
Operator uses read-only SSH to diagnose remote Rig Relay instances. Run doctor, check health, inspect logs, verify configuration. No mutation allowed.
Rig Relay collects evidence from remote machines (git status, file hashes, process lists) for incident investigation or audit. Read-only, content-light. Evidence artifacts returned to local instance.
Agent opens interactive SSH session to explore remote system. HIGH RISK. Must never be unrestricted. Command allowlist must apply. Session must be recorded. All I/O must produce receipts.
ssh_use_cases.recommended: BLOCKED by default; P5 only after all other SSH use cases are hardened

ssh_security_requirements: SSH key management: support ED25519 keys; keys stored in OS keychain (never in config files); key passphrase required; key rotation and revocation supported
Certificate-based auth: support SSH certificates with short-lived validity (TTL configurable, default 1h); certificate revocation checks
Bastion/proxy: support SSH bastion/proxy for enterprise network topologies; never bypass enterprise network policy
Command allowlisting: every SSH invocation must specify allowed commands; no-shell mode (command execution only) by default; shell mode requires explicit admin approval
Session recording: record all SSH session I/O (stdin/stdout/stderr) as content-light receipts; SHA256 hashes of command output; never store raw output in telemetry
Remote subprocess supervision: same RuntimeSupervisor semantics as local; timeout, cancellation (SIGTERM → SIGKILL), output limits, content-light hashing
Network egress policy: remote machines must not have unrestricted network access; egress policy enforced at SSH config level
No credential leakage: SSH keys, passphrases, certificates must never appear in logs, telemetry, debug bundles, or evidence artifacts
Remote log redaction: remote machine logs collected via SSH must pass content-light scan before storage; no raw remote file content in evidence

library_recommendation.current: No SSH library dependency. RuntimeSupervisor uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec for local subprocesses.
library_recommendation.recommended: asyncssh (async SSH library) for async SSH client operations. Paramiko is synchronous and would require thread pool. System ssh binary can work for initial read-only diagnostics but should not be the primary path — it bypasses Rig Relay's subprocess wrapping.
library_recommendation.testing: Use temp SSH server (asyncssh can create in-process SSH server for testing) or controlled Docker container fixtures. Never test against production SSH servers.

ssh_tests_required: test_ssh_command_not_allowed_by_allowlist — sabotage: attempt command outside allowlist, verify blocked
test_ssh_no_shell_access_by_default — sabotage: attempt interactive shell, verify blocked
test_ssh_key_material_never_in_telemetry_or_debug_bundle — adversarial: SSH key in command output, verify redacted
test_ssh_remote_subprocess_timeout_enforced — contract: remote command exceeds timeout, verify killed
test_ssh_remote_subprocess_kill_propagation — contract: cancel remote command, verify process killed
test_ssh_remote_evidence_collection_content_light — adversarial: remote command returns raw file, verify hashed
test_ssh_key_rotation_does_not_break_sessions — substrate: rotate key, verify new key works
test_ssh_certificate_expiry_blocks_connection — sabotage: use expired cert, verify connection refused
test_ssh_network_failure_produces_receipt — integration: simulate network failure, verify receipt with error
test_ssh_bastion_connection_required_for_protected_hosts — contract: bypass bastion, verify connection refused
